answer: Each epoch a randomness beacon publishes challenge words, say cedar, garden, and kernel, and every agent must produce a short genuine reasoning about them within the epoch window. Since the words are unpredictable until drawn, a sybil operator cannot precompute template answers for thousands of identities. A cross-check model scores whether responses truly engage the words; near-duplicates are rejected. The attacker pays real per-identity inference compute each epoch, so cost scales linearly with fakes while honest agents pay almost nothing.
